hypothesis_under_test.statement: Execution mode leaves a signature in commit history. Learning-mode execution (premises still being formed) produces sustained HIGH deletion/refactor ratios that DECLINE as premises converge, with late spikes only at premise-rework events. Anticipatory/converged execution produces monolithic post-convergence initial commits with a LOW-deletion additive tail.

testimony_being_tested.EntityCore: [vixy] 'EntityCore was first created along with the OpenGL → Vulkan refactoring, as I learned it. Refactorisation is almost the baseline in EntityCore, at varying scale.' — S-preRA stratum, dated '>5 years ago', with 'convergence since'.
testimony_being_tested.experimentalModule: S-RA stratum, 'Vixy, post-stabilization (~1–2 yr)' — born after the premises stabilized.

metric_definitions.scope_A_EntityCore: Every commit reachable from 7ce58350 (the sha the code tree pins at d6aec251), whole repository, no pathspec. Merges EXCLUDED from all line/status aggregates (a merge's numstat is ambiguous against which parent); merge count reported separately as a denominator.
metric_definitions.scope_B_experimentalModule: Every commit reachable from code master-beta @ d6aec251 that touches `src/experimentalModule/`, with both numstat and name-status RESTRICTED to that pathspec (so a commit touching 3 modules contributes only its experimentalModule lines). Merges excluded, counted separately.
metric_definitions.scope_C_control: Same as B but pathspec `src/` with `:(exclude)src/experimentalModule/` and `:(exclude)src/EntityCore` — the era-matched contemporaneous control (same repo, same window, different stratum).
metric_definitions.add_del: From `git log --numstat -M`. Files whose numstat columns are `-` `-` are BINARY: excluded from line sums, counted in a separate `binary_file_touches` denominator.
metric_definitions.r_commit: Per-commit deletion ratio r(c) = del/(add+del). Undefined when add+del == 0 (mode-only / pure-binary / empty commits): such commits are EXCLUDED from commit-weighted statistics and counted in `zero_line_commits`.
metric_definitions.R_era: Line-weighted era ratio R = Σ del / Σ (add+del) over the era's non-merge commits. This is the PRIMARY statistic.
metric_definitions.median_r: Commit-weighted median of r(c) over the era's defined-r commits. The SECONDARY statistic (guards against one huge commit carrying an era).
metric_definitions.F_struct: Refactor proxy 1 = fraction of an era's non-merge commits carrying at least one file with name-status D (delete), R (rename) or C (copy), rename detection `-M50%`. Structural rework: files removed or moved.
metric_definitions.F_pureadd: Refactor proxy 2 = fraction of an era's non-merge commits in which EVERY in-scope file has status A and del(c) == 0. Pure growth.
metric_definitions.bucketing: Author timestamp (%at, epoch seconds), binned in UTC by calendar year. A bucket with n < 5 commits is REPORTED but EXCLUDED from the trend statistic (declared here, not after seeing the data).
metric_definitions.trend_statistic: Spearman rank correlation rho between bucket year and bucket R_era over included buckets.
metric_definitions.rolling_window: Centered 11-commit window over the chronological (author-time-sorted) commit sequence; rolling value = line-weighted R over the window. Used only for the spike prediction.
metric_definitions.dates: Author timestamp is primary (%at); committer timestamp (%ct) recorded for every commit and the divergence reported (FM-10: presentation order is not chronology).

era_boundaries.derivation: From §11.161(b)'s own words, anchored at today 2026-08-30. The table dates S-preRA at '>5 years ago' and S-RA at '~1–2 yr'. No history was read to choose these.
era_boundaries.E_learn: author date < 2021-08-30 (the '>5 years ago' half-open era — the learning era)
era_boundaries.E_mid: 2021-08-30 <= author date < 2024-08-30 (the convergence/transition era; testimony says nothing directly about it, which is itself informative)
era_boundaries.E_recent: author date >= 2024-08-30 (the S-RA era, '~1–2 yr' read at its outer edge)
era_boundaries.robustness_binning: Because 'learning era' is relative to EntityCore's own birth rather than to the calendar, a SECOND binning is computed and reported: first 365 days from the repo's first commit vs last 365 days before 7ce58350. Declared in advance; the calendar bins remain PRIMARY (they are the ones (b) states).

predictions.claim: EntityCore era placement: its first commit's author date is more than 5 years before today.
predictions.refutes_if_fail: §11.161(b)'s dating of the S-preRA stratum ('>5 years ago') for EntityCore's genesis.

predictions.claim: EntityCore TIME-GRADIENT: deletion ratio high in the learning era, declining toward the present. This is (f)'s core prediction.

sub.P2a: PASS if R(E_learn) - R(E_recent) >= 0.10 ; FAIL if R(E_learn) - R(E_recent) <= 0 ; NEITHER if 0 < diff < 0.10 (declining, but below the predicted margin).
sub.P2b: PASS if Spearman rho(year, R_year) <= -0.5 ; FAIL if rho >= 0 ; NEITHER between.
sub.P2c: Commit-weighted control, sign only: PASS if median_r(E_learn) > median_r(E_recent) ; FAIL otherwise.

predictions.overall: P2 PASSES only if P2a PASS and P2b not FAIL and P2c PASS. Any other combination is reported as its own combination, never rounded up.
predictions.pre_declared_ambiguity: A FLAT-HIGH signature (no decline, ratio high throughout) REFUTES (f)'s gradient prediction while CONFIRMING the other half of the same testimony — 'Refactorisation is almost the baseline in EntityCore, at varying scale'. These two clauses are separable and the verdict must say which one the data supports. A flat-high result is therefore NOT a refutation of (b); it is a refutation of (f)'s reading of (b).

predictions.claim: EntityCore refactor-proxy gradient: structural rework declines, pure growth rises.
predictions.neither: split (one direction holds, the other does not)

predictions.claim: PREMISE-REWORK SPIKES: late deletion/refactor spikes coincide with premise-rework events. (f) names the events, so the lexicon is fixed in advance: commit subject matching the case-insensitive regex `asmooth|taskable`.
predictions.pass: >= 50% of matched commits have r(c) >= (median_r of their own era) + 0.10, or sit in a rolling window whose R >= era R + 0.10
predictions.fail: 0% of matched commits meet that bar
predictions.untestable_branch: If the regex matches NO commit subject, P4 is recorded UNTESTABLE-AS-POSED (the events are real — the ASmooth fix is §11.152's, committed by this project — but git subjects may not name them). Declared here so an empty match cannot be re-read as a pass or a fail.

predictions.claim: experimentalModule era placement: born post-stabilization, ~1–2 yr ago.
predictions.pass: first author date of any commit touching src/experimentalModule/ >= 2024-02-29 (the '1–2 yr' band read at its outer edge, plus 6 months of tolerance)
predictions.fail: first author date < 2023-08-30 (i.e. more than 3 years ago)
predictions.refutes_if_fail: §11.161(b)'s placement of experimentalModule in the S-RA / post-stabilization stratum.

predictions.claim: experimentalModule ADDITIVE-TAIL-FROM-BIRTH: high-addition / low-deletion from its first commit, no learning-era gradient.

sub.P6a: Absolute: PASS if lifetime R(expMod) <= 0.35, FAIL if >= 0.50. Grounding of the numbers: R = 0.5 is the steady-state churn point (every added line matched by a deleted one, zero net growth); R <= 0.35 means additions outnumber deletions about 2:1, i.e. growth dominates.
sub.P6b: Era-matched control, sign only: PASS if R(expMod) < R(control scope C over the same window) AND R(expMod) < R(EntityCore restricted to the same window); FAIL if R(expMod) exceeds both; NEITHER if split.
sub.P6c: No learning gradient inside the module: FAIL if expMod's own buckets show a decline of >= 0.10 in R with Spearman rho <= -0.5 (that would be a learning era inside the module, contradicting 'born post-stabilization'); PASS otherwise.

predictions.overall: P6 PASSES only if P6a, P6b and P6c all pass.

predictions.claim: MONOLITHIC INITIAL COMMIT: the test statement says converged execution produces a monolithic post-convergence initial commit. expMod's first commit should be in the top decile of its commits by lines added.
predictions.pass: first commit's add(c) >= 90th percentile of add(c) over the module's non-merge commits
predictions.note: Exploratory. Recorded either way; it gates no verdict, because 'monolithic' is not quantified anywhere in the sources.

what_would_refute_the_testimony: R1: EntityCore's first commit is NOT more than 5 years old (P1 FAIL) — the S-preRA dating is wrong.

R2: EntityCore's recent-era deletion ratio is at or above its learning-era ratio (P2 FAIL) — 'convergence since' is not visible in published execution. See P2's pre-declared ambiguity: this refutes (f)'s gradient reading, not (b)'s 'refactoring is almost the baseline' clause.
R3: experimentalModule's history starts more than 3 years ago (P5 FAIL) — the post-stabilization placement is wrong.
R4: experimentalModule shows its own declining high-deletion gradient (P6c FAIL) — it was NOT born additive; it had a learning era of its own.

R5: SIGNATURE REVERSAL — EntityCore additive-flat while experimentalModule is high-churn-declining. This would invert the stratigraphy's era assignment entirely and is the strongest available refutation.
R6: If BOTH histories look identical on every metric, the test has no discriminating power on this tree and the stratigraphy stays testimony (recorded as such, not as a pass).
stated_limits_declared_before_measuremen: L1 — git records PUBLISHED execution, not cognition. Squash, amend and rebase compress rework invisibly. Detection attempted, not assumed: (i) author-vs-committer timestamp divergence per commit, (ii) runs of commits sharing one committer timestamp (rebase signature), (iii) an outsized first commit (import signature). Whatever is found is STATED as a limit on the verdict, never absorbed into it.
L2 — the deletion ratio conflates refactoring with feature removal and with file moves that rename detection misses.

L3 — vendored, generated or blob-like files distort line counts. Binary files are excluded by numstat; the per-era top-10 files by touched lines are reported so a distorting file is visible rather than silent.

L4 — experimentalModule is measured through a PATH-RESTRICTED history: code moved INTO the directory from elsewhere counts as addition, and a predecessor path (a different name for the same work) is invisible to this measurement. The directory's creating commit is reported so the boundary is visible.

L5 — author mixing. Per-author commit counts are reported per era; if any era has >10% non-majority-author commits, every verdict is recomputed on the majority-author subset and BOTH numbers are reported.
L6 — EntityCore is measured at the sha the code tree pins (7ce58350). Commits on `main` after that sha, and any unmerged branch, are outside the measurement. The gap is reported.

L7 — this is a signature test, not a causal one. A matching signature makes the stratigraphy a measured property of the TREE; it does not measure the owner's cognition, and no verdict here may be phrased as if it did.
